title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Saudi Higher Education Administration
abstract: This study examines how the Saudi higher education administration is affected by the digital transformation, with a particular emphasis on student services management, data management, communication, administrative effectiveness, and decision-making. A representative sample of 930 administrative staff and information technology (IT) personnel from (6) public and private universities including; (Hail, Majmaah, Prince Satam bin Abdel- Aziz, Prince Sultan, Prince Meqren, and El-Faisal) universities, were given structured surveys as part of the research's quantitative, cross-sectional design, which was informed by the Technology-Organization-Environment paradigm. The results showed that digital transformation greatly improves decision-making and administrative efficiency, especially for administrative staff and in public universities. There are significant distinctions in staff positions and institutional types, meanwhile, with leadership seeing larger transformation advantages and public institutions benefiting more from government-backed efforts than IT professionals. title: When Giftedness Masks Need: Systemic Support and Organizational Conditions for Twice-Exceptional Students
abstract: This study investigated the identification, understanding, and support of twice-exceptional students—learners demonstrating above-average abilities alongside learning, emotional, or behavioural challenges—in Slovenian primary schools, with a focus on systemic and organizational conditions shaping support practices. A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted using an online survey administered to 115 educational professionals, including classroom teachers, special education teachers, inclusive pedagogues, and school counsellors. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods. Findings indicate that cognitive characteristics of twice-exceptional students are most consistently recognized, whereas socio-emotional and behavioural traits are frequently underestimated. Approximately 50–60% of students remain unidentified, primarily due to insufficient professional training, limited diagnostic tools, and fragmented institutional coordination. Current support practices focus predominantly on remediating learning difficulties, while fostering students’ strengths remains inconsistent. title: Kindergarten Teachers’ Perspectives on Sustainable Development: Insights from Early Childhood Education in Kindergartens
abstract: The role of kindergarten teachers in shaping young children's understanding of sustainability is crucial. This research aims to understand preschool teachers' perceptions of sustainability and evaluate their practices in the classroom. The sample consisted of 16 early education teachers. In this study, data collected using a semi-structured interview form were analyzed using the thematic analysis method. Through in-depth interviews, researchers can interact directly with the research subjects and explore the thoughts and feelings of the interviewees through questions and follow-ups. Thematic analysis is a flexible method widely preferred in qualitative research, allowing for in-depth interpretation of the meaning and essence of the data. This type of research is rare in Majmaah, Saudi Arabia. The research is a basic descriptive qualitative research. The results revealed that teachers' approaches to sustainability and the individual measures they take for a sustainable life fall under four main themes: economic, environmental, social, and cultural. The participants' emphasis on the importance of starting sustainability education at an early age and connecting children with nature ca

title: Effectiveness of Game-Based Learning (GBL) Approach on Students’ Learning Outcomes in Mathematics Education: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: This study conducted a meta-analysis of 23 empirical studies (k = 23) (during the period 2010-2025) to evaluate the effectiveness of game-based learning (GBL) on student learning outcomes in Mathematics. The pooled results indicate that GBL has a positive and significant impact compared to traditional teaching methods, yielding a substantial overall effect size of Hedges’s g = 0.651 (95% CI: 0.304 to 0.998, p < 0.001). This effect is especially evident when GBL is systematically integrated and aligned with learning objectives. In addition to improving academic scores and problem-solving skills, the findings suggest that GBL enhances learners' motivation and engagement. However, the study identified several important moderating factors, including game type, student age, and pedagogical implementation. This analysis provides strong empirical evidence supporting GBL as an effective tool in mathematics education and offers strategic recommendations for educators and developers to optimize its impact.

title: Integrating the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals into English Language Programs: A Case Study
abstract: The integration of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into higher education is increasingly recognized as vital to advancing sustainable development worldwide. While Saudi universities have shown a strong institutional commitment to sustainability, there is still limited evidence of how these goals are incorporated at the program level, especially in non-STEM disciplines. This qualitative case study examines how well the SDGs are embedded in the Bachelor of Arts in English Language program at Majmaah University, a national leader in sustainability efforts. Data were gathered through document analysis of program specifications, operational and training plans, and community partnership documents, as well as semi-structured interviews with faculty members. Results reveal that although graduate attributes suggestively align with SDG-related skills such as critical thinking, intercultural communication, and social responsibility, explicit inclusion of the SDGs in learning outcomes, teaching methods, and assessments remains scarce. Implementation largely depends on individual faculty efforts rather than on institutional policies, and professional development opportun

title: Integrating Technology in Mathematics Classrooms: A Case Study of Scientific Calculator Use in Secondary Schools
abstract: The educational system in Malaysia needs to improve calculator implementation because schools must fulfill their responsibility of developing Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) through national regulations. This research study examines the link between scientific calculator competencies and the Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) performance of Form Four students who solve quadratic functions. A secondary school in Johor conducted a primarily quantitative research study with supplementary qualitative elements (open-ended questionnaire responses), involving 55 students who completed the Calculator Competency Test (α = 0.89), the HOTS Assessment (α = 0.91), and the student questionnaire (α = 0.85). The findings showed a strong positive association between calculator proficiency and HOTS performance (r = 0.949, p < 0.001). The regression results (R² = 0.901) are exploratory due to the small sample size (n = 55); this should be interpreted as a preliminary association rather than a predictive relationship. title: Evaluating Students’ Attitudes towards Blended Intensive Programmes: Impact on Intercultural Competences and Digital Collaboration
abstract: Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs) represent a key innovation within the Erasmus+ programme, supporting internationalization by integrating virtual collaboration with short-term physical mobility. This format expands access to global learning opportunities while strengthening digital skills, intercultural competence, and multidisciplinary cooperation. This article focuses on students’ attitudes towards BIPs across 17 European and international higher education institutions from 13 countries. Utilizing pre- and post-intervention survey data, the research evaluates participants’ intercultural competencies, digital literacy, communication confidence, and collaborative skills. The study also assesses future engagement, perceived value, overall satisfaction, and project challenges. Analysis reveals statistically significant positive changes in students’ attitudes towards internationalization and their soft skills following BIP participation. Students also evaluated the experience as innovative and valuable, with many indicating an intention to participate in future programs. In addition to quantitative analysis, qualitative feedback collected through student interviews provides further

title: The Effect of Student Ability Labels on Teachers’ Perceptions of Problem Posing in Mathematics Education
abstract: Researchers conducted a survey (N = 157) to test whether student ability labels affect teachers’ perceptions and use of problem posing, an instructional strategy in which students generate mathematical questions and problems. The researchers hypothesized that teachers generally consider problem posing to be more concept-oriented than routine problem solving, and that teachers asked to consider students labelled “high-achieving” would be more likely to use problem posing than those asked about students labelled “low-achieving.” Consistent with previous research, secondary mathematics teachers viewed problem posing as a mainly concept-oriented strategy that promotes higher-order thinking. By a sizable margin, teachers were significantly more likely to support the use of problem posing when asked about high-performing students. Teachers asked about low achieving students reported being significantly less likely to use problem-posing tasks. Differences in use of strategies like problem posing could contribute to achievement gaps in mathematics as research has shown that problem-posing tasks are differentiable for and accessible to students who have previously demonstrated struggle in m

title: Impact of Digital and Non-Digital Educational Games on Grade 1 Students’ Engagement and Academic Achievement
abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital (online) and non-digital (offline) educational games on academic achievement and student engagement among Grade 1 learners in mathematics and geography, drawing on constructivist learning principles and self-determination theory to frame how game-based activities support autonomy, competence, and relatedness. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was employed with two intact classes (N = 50) from a public school in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Students were assigned to either an online game-based instructional condition or an offline game-based condition, and both groups participated in six weeks of structured game-integrated lessons. Data were collected through academic assessments, engagement checklists, motivation surveys, and teacher observations. Results show that both digital and non-digital games produced measurable gains in mathematics and geography scores, with the online group demonstrating slightly higher improvement percentages; however, independent t-tests indicated no statistically significant differences between groups (p > 0.05, d = 0.12–0.18). Engagement and motivation remained high across both conditions, with offline

title: The Degree to which Special Education Teachers Possess Procedural Research Skills
abstract: The current study examined the degree to which special education teachers possess procedural research skills. While previous studies have mainly focused on assessing the level of procedural research skills possession among general education teachers, this study particularly explores this context among special education teachers, closing a gap in the literature where, to the best of the researcher’s knowledge, only one exists in Al Qassim region. A quantitative research method was utilized. Participants consisted of 172 special education teachers. The data were collected from participants via a researcher-developed questionnaire consisting of 40 items distributed across five subdimensions, representing one of the significant contributions of the current research as a reliable tool for similar future researchers. To answer the study questions, data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS, version 26), employing descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages), Cronbach's alpha, Pearson's correlation, and MANCOVA. Results revealed a low level of procedural research skills possession among special education teachers. In addition, there were no signific

title: Students’ Motivations for Multilingual Programmes with EMI or DMI vs. Unilingual Programmes in French
abstract: English Medium Instruction (EMI) programmes have been rapidly expanding in higher education, and students’ motivations for enrolling in such programmes have been described in various studies. However, programmes taught in Languages Other Than English (LOTE) in higher education also exist, and it remains unclear whether students’ motivations for enrolling in these programmes differ from those observed in EMI contexts. This paper addresses this gap by analysing the motivations of students enrolled in three different study programmes in French-speaking Belgium: (1) multilingual programmes including Dutch Medium Instruction (DMI), (2) multilingual programmes with English (EMI), and (3) unilingual programmes (French only). 706 Bachelor’s degree students took part in an online survey, in which motivation was assessed through a series of items based on the expectancy-value model of achievement (Eccles & Wigfield, 2002). Using a cluster analysis, the findings reveal distinct motivation profiles across study programmes, varying according to students’ socio-economic status and linguistic background. Multilingual programmes have more students who see high value and interest in their study pro

title: Mixed Belief System of Mexican University Teachers about Assessment in Mathematics Classrooms: An Instrumental and Exploratory Case Study
abstract: Teachers' beliefs about mathematics assessment have been a topic of growing interest worldwide in the field of mathematics education. However, there are few studies conducted with higher education teachers, since research has focused on elementary and middle school levels. With the aim of identifying and characterizing beliefs about assessment of Mexican university mathematics teachers, a field study was conducted with a qualitative approach and an exploratory level of depth, using an instrumental case study design. For the collection of information, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 teachers who decided to participate voluntarily. The findings go beyond the binary classification of productive and unproductive beliefs, revealing a complex system of “mixed beliefs.” While teachers discursively value formative assessment, institutional pressures and traditional epistemological orientations generate significant tensions, resulting in a reliance on summative practices. Additionally, beliefs related to affective factors and the application of mathematical knowledge emerged inductively. These differences appear to be related to teaching experience and academic background,

title: Coping Beyond Inclusion: A Narrative Inquiry into Stress and Coping among Visually Impaired Students in Nepal
abstract: This study aims to explore how VI students develop coping strategies within an inclusive mainstream school in Nepal, and the purpose of this study is to interpret them through the theoretical lenses of “Stress and Coping” and Hindu cultural beliefs. The study employed a narrative research design. Four VI students at the secondary level were purposively selected from two inclusive schools based on having visual impairments, enrolment in secondary level (grades 9 to 12), and willingness to participate with consent. Semi-structured interviews were conducted using open-ended questions. This study reveals that coping is a dynamic and evolving process that unfolds through interaction with challenges, continuous appraisal of challenges, access to and use of available resources, and the construction of meaning over time in the social, cultural, and institutional context. To overcome the challenges and survive in school education, VI students develop and adopt several coping strategies. Among them, peer support, self-resilience, utilization of modern technologies, familiarizing with the surroundings, and active listening and memorization play a central role. title: The Effects of Educational Mobile Games on improving Critical Thinking Skills in Preschool Children
abstract: The aim was to Improve critical thinking skills in preschool children in Saudi Arabiathrough the use of educational mobile games. To study whether the data of the experimental group and the control group are significantly different in the pre-test and post-test mean of interpretation, explanation, evaluation, inference, analysis, and self-regulation. The research for this situation uses an independent sample T-test and an independent sample. The study was conducted with 60 students aged 4-6 attending a public school in Majmaaha city. 30 students were included in the experimental group from among the 60 students (30+30) in the two classes using simple random sampling, ensuring an equal chance of selection for each child. Findings revealed that including educational games in the teaching process, in addition to the teaching activities required by the current preschool education program, improves critical thinking skills. A significant difference was found in favor of the experimental group in the sub-dimensions of critical thinking, namely explanation, interpretation, inference, analysis, and self-regulation skills.

title: Different Types of Teacher Feedback on Student Errors in Whole-class Interaction
abstract: In recent pedagogical discourse, errors are understood as opportunities for learning. Increasing research has provided evidence about the relationship between the quality of student-teacher interaction and learning outcomes. Consequently, the role of teacher feedback during interaction is especially critical, particularly in error situations where the learning process can be supported. This research focuses on teachers’ feedback during whole-class interaction in the Czech language classes. The research question is: 'How do teachers support students by providing feedback on students’ errors during whole-class discourse?' The study was designed as a qualitative investigation, with data collected through classroom observations and interviews with teachers (N=4). Four teachers from ninth grade participated in the study, with six lessons observed for each teacher (N=24). Data analysis was based on linguistic ethnography, accompanied by inductive coding. Based on the empirical data and an analysis of error situations (N = 153), two types of teacher feedback on student errors resulting from student misunderstanding were distinguished. title: Digitized Project-Based Learning in Senior High School Statistics: An Integration of Mathematics and Climate Change Education
abstract: This study explored the development and validation of a digitized project-based learning material. This is guided by the cross-disciplinary approach in teaching senior high school statistics using local climate concepts. Anchored on Constructivism Learning Theory, this study was conducted using developmental research design, which comprised three sequential and interdependent stages: analysis, design and development, and validation and evaluation. For the analysis and design development stages, two science teachers, two statistics teachers, two climate change experts, one educational technology expert, and one project-based learning expert were purposively selected and participated in the two stages of interview. Using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis, seven themes emerged: integrated statistics and climate competence for informed action, active, collaborative, and technology-enhanced project-based approaches, comprehensive, authentic, and reflective project-based assessment, purposeful and scaffolded project-based learning, interactive and visual interface design, usability and accessibility features, and real-time feedback and support systems. title: Pre-school Leaders’ Perspectives on Foreign Language Education
abstract: The introduction of foreign language (FL) learning in pre-school education has gained increasing attention across Europe and beyond; however, in many contexts it remains weakly regulated and largely dependent on local initiatives. In Slovenia, FL education is not formally embedded in the national pre-school curriculum, placing pre-school leaders in a key position as mediators between policy frameworks, parental expectations, and pedagogical practice. Despite their central role, empirical research on their perspectives remains limited. This study examined pre-school leaders’ views on the organization, implementation, and quality of FL teaching in Slovenian pre-schools. A quantitative survey design was employed using an online questionnaire completed by 162 pre-school leaders. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis of open-ended responses. The findings showed that FL provision was present in 54.9% of pre-schools and was predominantly organised as an optional enrichment activity rather than as part of the regular programme. English dominated the language offer (82%), and FL teaching was frequently delivered by external providers. While leaders

title: Implementing the Integrated Foreign Languages Curriculum in Greek EFL Education: Teachers’ Beliefs, Practices and Professional Challenges
abstract: This article examines Greek EFL teachers’ beliefs, training experiences, and reported classroom practices in implementing the Integrated Foreign Languages Curriculum (IFLC, hereafter) — a nationwide curriculum innovation introduced in Greek state schools as part of a broader reform agenda to modernize foreign language education. Drawing on English foreign language (EFL, hereafter) teachers’ beliefs, training and practices, the study explores how teachers mediate top-down curricular change within complex institutional realities. Employing a mixed-methods design, quantitative data from 370 EFL teachers were triangulated with semi-structured interviews with 16 EFL teachers and 8 school advisors, alongside the analysis of 12 lesson plans. The findings reveal limited awareness and fragmented training, resulting in partial and uneven implementation of the IFLC. While many teachers endorse the innovation’s communicative and learner-centered philosophy, deeply entrenched beliefs, contextual constraints, and insufficient professional support hinder full implementation. Nonetheless, emerging evidence of adaptive and selective agency suggests teachers’ gradual movement toward more reflective

title: STEM-Integrated VR/AR Learning for Enhancing Students’ Critical Thinking: Evidence from a Single-Class Study
abstract: This study aims to examine the role of STEM-integrated Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) learning in enhancing students’ critical thinking skills. Critical thinking is an essential competency, particularly in STEM disciplines, where students are required to analyze information, evaluate evidence, and solve complex problems. However, international assessments suggest that students’ critical thinking abilities remain relatively underdeveloped, especially in subjects such as chemistry, where many concepts are abstract and difficult to visualize. A quasi-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design was employed to evaluate students’ critical thinking skills. Participants completed a pretest prior to engaging with the STEM-AR/VR learning intervention and a posttest afterward to measure any changes in performance. The results indicated a statistically significant improvement in students’ critical thinking skills, with overall significance (2-tailed) values below 0.05. These findings contribute to the growing body of research on immersive educational technologies and highlight the potential of STEM-integrated VR/AR learning environments to support higher-order thinking ski

title: The Impact of Flipped Learning on Writing Autonomy and Expository Essay Writing Ability
abstract: This research is aimed to investigate the effect of Flipped Learning (FL) on grade 9 students’ writing autonomy and expository essay writing ability. A quasi-experimental pre-test post-test design was employed, and involved 103 students from Fasiledes No. 2 Secondary School in Gondar town. Of the total, 51 students were assigned to experimental group, and 52 students to the conventional group. The design spanned 12 weeks. The validated writing autonomy scale and expository essay writing test were used. The structural Equation Modelling analysis shows that FL statistically predicted writing autonomy (R2=.612, β = .533. SE=.067, 95% CI [.42, .67], P=.001) and expository essay writing ability (R2=.359, β = .539. SE=.067, 95% CI [.39, .66], P=.001). Writing autonomy also statistically predicted expository essay writing ability (R2=.516, β = .411. SE=.047, 95% CI [.32, .50], P=.001), and partially mediated the relationship between FL and expository essay writing ability. This study recommends using flipped learning in writing classes can improve students’ writing autonomy. title: Middle School Students’ Perceptions of Learning the Periodic Table with an AI Chatbot: A Gender Perspective
abstract: This study investigated students' perceptions of using an AI-based chatbot featuring Marie Curie in Chemistry education. This study involved two 9th-grade classes in Lisbon (N = 37) and followed a concurrent mixed methods design.A questionnaire with seven closed-ended questions and one open-ended question was used. The data analysis methodologies applied included descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, and content analysis. Quantitative data revealed that students found the development of competencies such as reasoning, information processing, scientific knowledge, and critical thinking to be adequate, though interpersonal skills development was less evident. No statistically significant gender differences were found. Qualitative analysis identified main categories with gendered patternThe findings indicate that integrating an AI-based educational chatbot into Chemistry lessons was perceived as clear and engaging, highlighting its potential to enhance STEM learning and promote female role models, while underscoring the need for collaborative methodologies to foster relational skills.

title: Structured Course Generation for Kinect-based Chinese Character Learning: A Prerequisite-Driven Approach for Improved Learning
abstract: Learning Chinese characters is challenging for non-native speakers due to their complex visual structures and weak phonetic correspondence. Although gesture-based interactive systems have been proposed to enhance engagement, they often lack structured course plans, leading to cognitive overload and inefficient learning. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a systematic course generation method for a Kinect-based Chinese character educational system. The method first decomposes characters into multi-granularity learning objects. It then constructs a prerequisite structure based on inclusion relationships and assigns difficulty levels according to structural complexity. An easy-to-complex learning path is subsequently generated using topological sorting. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a controlled user study involving 40 non-native learners is conducted, which compares a guided learning mode (Treatment) with an unguided mode (Control). The results demonstrate that the Treatment group significantly outperforms the Control group in written performance, perceived cognitive load, system usefulness, and learning satisfaction (P < 0.05). title: Sociolinguistic Functions of First Language Use in Conversation-Based EFL Lessons: Class Observation in the Slovak EFL Context
abstract: This study explores the sociolinguistic role of the first language (L1) in a conversation focused English as a Foreign Language (EFL) lesson. Drawing on a qualitative observational design, the research is based on an overt, non participatory observation of a single 90 minute lesson delivered to 16 B2 level students at an eight year grammar school in Slovakia. Field notes and an event based timeline were used to document instances of L1 use across instructional phases and activity types, and a short post lesson survey triangulated learners’ perceptions of authenticity and communicative value. The analysis examines how L1 functions across different classroom settings, its frequency, and the sociolinguistic factors driving code switching. Findings reveal that L1 use is most frequent during non formal, peer oriented tasks such as role play and speed questioning, where it supports solidarity, humor, and pragmatic flexibility. Teacher led phases employ L1 strategically for scaffolding and clarification, while formal assessment contexts remain L1 free. title: Integrating Critical Thinking and Mathematical Inquiry: A Framework for Instruction in Ordinary Differential Equations
abstract: Critical thinking is widely recognised as a core educational objective in higher educa-tion. This study examined how undergraduate students’ critical thinking can be en-hanced through mathematics by proposing a teaching framework that integrates critical thinking with mathematical inquiry in the context of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). A quasi-experimental mixed-methods design was employed with 98 students from one university, combining quantitative and qualitative data to investigate the ef-fects of different instructional approaches on students’ critical thinking development and ODE learning.The findings showed that inquiry-based instruction supported students’ conceptual understanding of ODEs and significantly improved their critical thinking skills. However, instructional approaches that explicitly infused critical thinking into inquiry-based instruction were more effective than implicit inquiry approaches in im-proving students’ overall critical thinking and ODE achievement. In addition, students’ critical thinking performance was strongly positively correlated with their ODE achievement. Qualitative findings further suggested that explicit critical thinking in-struc

title: Integrating Collaborative Digital Multimodal Composing in EFL Classrooms: A Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review investigates the integration of collaborative digital multimodal composing (CDMC) in EFL classrooms. Following the PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in Scopus, Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI), and EBSCO databases to identify 45 empirical studies published between 2013 and 2024. Data were extracted and synthesized using thematic synthesis. This paper identifies key trends, learning outcomes, and implementation challenges in diverse educational contexts. Findings reveal a significant increase in CDMC studies since 2020, predominantly in East Asian tertiary contexts. Task designs have evolved from digital storytelling to more complex multimedia and AI-enhanced compositions. Reported learning outcomes include improved writing proficiency, enhanced genre awareness, development of multimodal and digital literacy, and stronger collaborative skills. However, its implementation is hindered by insufficient teacher training in digital pedagogy, technological and infrastructural obstacles, curricular misalignments with traditional assessment, and complexities in managing student collaboration. title: Individual Performance Feedback Promotes Retrieval Practice Across Prior Knowledge Levels
abstract: This study aimed to examine whether individual performance feedback combined with retrieval practice influences students’ perceptions of its usefulness among learners with low and high prior knowledge. Retrieval practice is an effective study strategy that enhances long-term retention through active knowledge recall, although students often underestimate it and prefer passive strategies such as restudying. A total of 140 students participated, completing tests under both retrieval practice and restudy conditions. The results showed a significant effect in favor of retrieval practice on delayed tests. Furthermore, individual feedback positively influenced students’ beliefs about the strategy’s effectiveness, increasing its subsequent use. Regarding mental effort and judgments of learning, no significant findings were observed; however, feedback did enhance decision-making among those who experienced the testing effect, particularly in students with low prior knowledge. These findings suggest that providing individual performance feedback may help students better recognize the benefits of retrieval practice and promote more effective learning strategies.

title: Influencing Factors of Secondary Students’ Mathematical Communication Competence from Teachers’ Perspectives: An EFA-CFA Study
abstract: This study aims to identify and validate the latent factors influencing secondary students’ mathematical communication competence from the perspective of mathematics teachers in Vietnam. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 533 mathematics teachers and randomly split into two subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (EFA, n = 266) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA, n = 267). The results revealed a five-factor structure explaining 65.95% of the total variance, including teaching methods and models, students’ individual characteristics, mathematical communication competence, classroom environment and interactions, and learning resources and support tools. CFA results confirmed good model fit and established reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. These findings contribute to the identification and preliminary validation of a context-specific measurement model. Practically, the results provide a provide a basis for designing instructional strategies and improving classroom practices to enhance students’ mathematical communication competence in alignment with Vietnam’s 2018 General Education Curriculum.

title: Teachers´ Self-efficacy - A Quantitative Study of the Impact of an Online Wellbeing Course
abstract: This study examines the impact of participation in an online wellbeing course on teachers’ perceived self-efficacy. A pre-test/post-test design was employed with a sample of 118 teachers. Data were collected using a five-subscale questionnaire adapted from the Norwegian Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale (NTES), assessing Instruction, Adaptation, Motivation, Discipline, and Cooperation. The findings indicate a positive effect of the online wellbeing course on four dimensions of teacher self-efficacy: Instruction, Adaptation, Motivation, and Discipline, suggesting that targeted online interventions can enhance key professional competencies. However, no significant changes were observed in the Cooperation dimension. Further analysis revealed a statistically significant relationship between teaching experience and the Cooperation subscale, indicating that more experienced teachers may perceive greater efficacy in collaborative practices. Overall, the results highlight the potential of online wellbeing training as an effective approach to supporting teachers’ self-efficacy, professional growth, and overall wellbeing. These findings contribute to discussions on teacher development and support.

title: Linking Personal Variables to Teacher Engagement within the Professional Teaching Competency Framework
abstract: In line with European educational policies, the development of a framework of professional teaching competences is essential to ensure quality teaching capable of responding to current social demands. Effective teaching requires sustained professional commitment throughout the teaching career, particularly within competence-based education. In this context, identifying key personal variables that contribute to educational effectiveness and quality is especially relevant. This study analyzes teaching commitment among active non-university teachers, focusing on the role of self-efficacy, emotional intelligence, and happiness as core personal factors. The sample included teachers from Secondary Education, Baccalaureate, and Vocational Training. A quantitative, descriptive, correlational, comparative, cross-sectional, and ex post facto research design was employed. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlational analysis, hierarchical linear regression, and mediation analysis. The results revealed significant relationships between the studied variables and teaching commitment, with self-efficacy emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by happiness and emotional int

title: Dialogic Interaction in Grammar Instruction: Exploring Explicit and Implicit Approaches in an EFL Classroom
abstract: This study examines the role of dialogic interaction in mediating explicit and implicit grammar instruction in an EFL classroom context. Despite growing emphasis on communicative approaches, grammar teaching at the tertiary level often remains teacher-directed and monologic. The study employed a mixed-methods design involving 100 EFL students (aged 16–18) at Fergana State University academic lyceum, randomly assigned to an explicit instruction group (n = 50) or an implicit instruction group (n = 50) over a 12-week intervention. Quantitative data were collected through pre-test and post-test grammar assessments and Likert-scale perception surveys, while qualitative data were gathered via semi-structured interviews and video-recorded classroom discourse. Results showed that the explicit instruction group achieved significantly higher grammatical accuracy gains (pre-test M = 62.40, post-test M = 78.90) compared to the implicit instruction group (pre-test M = 61.85, post-test M = 71.30), with a statistically significant between-group difference (t(98) = 4.12, p < .05, Cohen's d = 0.65). Qualitatively, dialogic interaction functioned as a pedagogic mediator in both conditions, facilitat

title: Beyond Intelligence: Construction and Validation of the Four-Dimensional Dynamic Model of Learning Competence
abstract: The "intelligence-achievement paradox" raises a fundamental question in educational research: why do students with comparable cognitive abilities often exhibit markedly different academic trajectories? While existing frameworks provide valuable insights into isolated predictors, they frequently lack an integrated mechanism to explain these disparities. This study develops and validates a Four-Dimensional Dynamic Model of Learning Competence—comprising Learning Capital, Strategy, Input, and Environment—to address this theoretical fragmentation. Employing an exploratory sequential mixed methods design within the context of Chinese higher education, we first conducted semi-structured interviews (N=18) to operationalize the model's dimensions. A subsequent survey of 524 undergraduates was utilized to validate the psychometric properties of the newly developed Learning Ability Four-Dimensional Diagnostic Scale (LA-FDDS). Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) indicates that Learning Strategy significantly mediates the relationship between Learning Capital and Input, accounting for 58.6% of the total effect, while the Learning Environment functions as a pivotal moderator. title: Perspectives of English Language Teachers on Fairness and Justice in Assessing Writing
abstract: Neglect of issues in fairness and justice in writing assessment has far-reaching consequences on teachers and learners, giving way to consider the role of teacher training courses, professional development, and psychological state in scoring students’ writings. The current qualitative study investigated Malaysian and Chinese English language teachers’ perspectives of justice and fairness in assessing writing in response to different tasks. The participants were selected purposively. Multiple methods were followed to collect the data. The participants performed two tasks, which involved them in (i) individually reading two short stories, one related to fairness and the other to justice according to Kunnan’s (2014) definition of the terms, (ii) writing their reflections about each task individually, and (iii) participating in group interviews. The findings indicated that participants were more confident about what constitutes justice than fairness. The participants’ educational backgrounds and upbringing revealed differences between the Chinese and Malaysian participants. The study has pedagogical and methodological implications.

title: The Availability and Utilization of Mathematics-Focused STEM Resources in Secondary School
abstract: Mathematics education is essential for advancing Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM), yet disparities in instructional resources persist in secondary schools across Pakistan. This study investigates the availability and utilization of mathematics-focused STEM resources in government and private, as well as urban and rural, secondary schools. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was adopted. Quantitative data were collected from 116 secondary mathematics teachers using a structured survey instrument, and internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Regression analysis was used to examine relationships among resource availability, institutional support, and instructional utilization. The quantitative results reveal significant disparities between urban private and rural public schools regarding both resource availability and pedagogical utilization. A strong positive association was found between resource availability and utilization, while contextual institutional factors also shaped implementation patterns. title: Examining Sound Animation of Visual Artworks and Its Connection to the Development of Rhythmic Sensitivity and Perception in Preschool Children
abstract: The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between sound animation of visual artworks and the development of rhythmic sensitivity and perception in preschool children. The study employed a qualitative action research design conducted in a kindergarten setting in Slovenia and involved 36 preschool children. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and analysis of children’s visual and musical products, and were analysed using thematic analysis. The results indicate that multisensory and interdisciplinary activities contribute to the development of rhythmic perception, creative expression, and the transfer of rhythm between visual and auditory modalities. The findings emphasise the importance of integrating music and visual arts in early childhood education.

title: German-Language Majors’ Voices on ChatGPT Use in Tertiary Education: A Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: This mixed-methods study examines how Ukrainian undergraduates majoring in German language studies perceive and use ChatGPT. 113 participants responded to the ChatGPT Usage Scale for Foreign Language Learners, developed by Çobanoğullari and Özbek (2025) and supplemented with open-ended questions to deepen understanding of students’ attitudes toward ChatGPT use. Quantitative results showed moderate to high levels of ChatGPT use in domains such as information retrieval, grammar explanations, and exam preparation. Students reported substantially lower engagement in higher-order activities, including the development of critical thinking, creativity, and communicative skills. Findings indicate significant demographic nuances: female students exhibited stronger affective and motivational engagement – suggesting AI’s role in maintaining academic continuity and resilience – while language proficiency level did not dictate frequency of use. Qualitative findings confirmed these patterns and highlighted perceived gains in efficiency, personalized support, and reduced anxiety, as well as concerns about inaccuracies and over-reliance. title: The Impact of a Curriculum-Based Measurement Instrument on the Reading Comprehension Performance of Students with Dyslexia
abstract: Dyslexia is a condition that is common among special education students. Dyslexia can cause many learning and psychological problems for students if not addressed early. The purpose of the study was to investigate the effect of a small group reading intervention on the reading comprehension proficiency of third grade students with dyslexia. In this study, the independent variable was inclusion in a small-group reading intervention. The dependent variable was reading comprehension, as measured by a series of Curriculum-Based Measurement (CBM) reading comprehension tests. The CBM is an assessment method which is used to monitor progress of students in basic academic areas. A special education teacher prepared all of the materials for these interventions and conducted them over the period of 25 school days. A multiple-baseline design was used to compare the timelines of the intervention’s effectiveness among different participants. Analysis of descriptive statistics and nonoverlap of all pairs (NAP) tests were used to explore the results of the intervention. title: Evaluation of a Long-Term In-Service English Teacher Training Program
abstract: The English Experts Program is one of the long-term in-service training programs at the Specialized Institute for Professional Training of Teachers. Despite its comprehensive design and national importance, the program has experienced limited participation rates and participant withdrawals. These issues necessitated a systematic evaluation to determine whether the program's intended objectives were being effectively achieved. Therefore, the current study aimed to investigate whether the objectives of the methodological part and the language proficiency part of the program have been attained from the participants’ perspective. In addition, it investigated the effects of variables such as gender, teaching experience, cohort, and teaching level on the achievement of the program’s objectives. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design was employed in this study. The data were collected through a questionnaire and a content analysis of the participants’ reflection reports. The study included participants from the first and the second cohorts. title: Humour in EFL Classes: Effects on Academic Engagement, Anxiety, and Language Learning
abstract: This research examined the impact of humour on English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learner’s educational engagement, their language skills, and their feelings of anxiety. To do this, the researchers created a quasi-experimental study. Thirty-six students studying in an English institute were asked to participate in this experimental study and completed two questionnaires. For assessing the participation behaviour of students, the engagement questionnaire designed by Golestani and Ghanizadeh (forthc.) was used to evaluate the three elements of engagement. It includes 24 items: The behavioural (9 items, Questions 1-9), emotional (3 items, Questions 10-12), and cognitive engagement (12 items, Questions 13-24) (Appendix A). To measure the anxiety of cross-cultural communication, six components from Dörnyei's L2 motivational self-system (2005), which were translated into Persian and validated in the Iranian context by Papi (2010), were used (Appendix B). title: Pedagogical Experiences among International Student Exchange Interns from Selected Higher Education in the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand
abstract: This qualitative study examines how international student-teacher interns enact day-to-day pedagogy during cross-border practicum placements under the SEA-Teacher Project of SEAMEO. Data were collected from eight interns representing higher education institutions in the Philippines (n = 4), Indonesia (n = 2), and Thailand (n = 2) and analysed using a narrative-informed thematic approach to capture both lived experience accounts and cross-case pedagogical patterns. Findings show that interns’ classroom practice was shaped by a dynamic interplay of instructional autonomy in lesson design, adaptive use of student-centered strategies, balancing structure and empathy in classroom management, and combining formative and summative assessment approaches. At the same time, pedagogical choices were constrained and redirected by institutional and structural conditions, curriculum expectations, material resources, infrastructure, pre-deployment preparation, and accommodation realities, together with communication and cultural adjustment demands. title: An Analytical Study of the Evolution of Online Learning in Teacher Education: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: This study explored online learning in teacher education regarding the use of technology and its access, equity and ethical issues during the COVID-19 disruption to teacher training within higher education, and how it has evolved. This qualitative study was underpinned by connectivism theory. Data was collected through interviews and questionnaire surveys involving ten educators and seven preservice teachers from various higher education institutions in England and Wales. The data was analyzed following thematic analysis. The themes generated included integrating a hybrid mode of teaching, redesign and restructure of the curriculum; resilience and adaptability; career progression; promoting innovation and digital literacy; digital inequality and gap in technology access; and the ethical issues regarding AI use. Evidence from the study shows that the digital divide resulting in inequalities in knowledge and skills in online learning and technology persists among institutions and teachers.
